newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares leap 2.82 pct on selective buys.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares leap 2.82 pct on selective buys.

text.p: Istanbul shares jumped an average 2.82 percent in selective activity led by blue chips on Tuesday morning following Monday's 1.47 percent down correction to the recent rally, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 gained 32 points to end at a new midday high of 1,168, compared to a previous midday record of 1,163 and an all-time high close of 1,153 on Friday.
Morning volume rose to 10.33 trillion lira from Monday's 7.74 trillion lira.
"Expectations remained up although Monday's correction was not strong enough. Volume fell sharply yesterday which also sparked reaction buys," said Hasan Soydan from Garanti investment.
Some brokers expect share-based activity to continue in the afternoon while other await some profit-taking.
The index had surged 18.1 percent, breaking record closes on seven consecutive days after the market reopened on January 2 following a five-day holiday.

Of the 238 shares traded, rises outdid falls sharply by 177 to 20 and 41 finished stable. The IMKB Industrial gained 2.17 percent to 1,226, the IMKB Services leapt 3.78 percent to 1,209 and the IMKB Finacial jumped 3.03 percent to 1,123.
